memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'He will tether his donkey to a vine, his colt to the choicest branch; he will wash his garments in wine, his robes in the blood of grapes. His eyes will be darker than wine, his teeth whiter than milk.'" — Gen 49:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These are pictures of extraordinary abundance. A land so rich in vines that you can tie your donkey to one and not care if it eats the branch. So much wine that you could wash your clothes in it. This is the poetry of a world overflowing.

Jacob is describing the prosperity of Judah's territory — but the language reaches beyond any patch of farmland. Scripture repeatedly uses overflowing wine as a picture of the age of God's Messiah (Amos 9:13; Isa 25:6).

And there is a detail here that a Christian cannot read without pausing. A donkey's colt, tethered and waiting. Centuries later, the King of Judah's line rode into Jerusalem on a donkey's colt, exactly as prophecy had said (Zech 9:9; Matt 21:5).

Jesus also began His public ministry by turning water into wine at a wedding — an abundance so extravagant that it embarrassed the host (Jn 2:1-11).

Be careful not to turn this into a promise of material wealth for believers. It is not. It is a picture of the richness of the age Christ brings, which we taste now and will know fully at the wedding supper of the Lamb (Rev 19:9).

The best wine is kept for last.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have you tasted the richness of life in Christ?
2. Do you look forward to what is coming, or only backwards?
3. How do you guard against turning God's promises into a promise of wealth?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the abundant life Christ brings, and for the feast still to come. Keep my heart set on the richness of knowing Him rather than on material things. Amen.
